source.title: In Search of Grandmother Cells: Tracing Interpretable Neurons in Tabular Representations

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether neurons are selective for individual concepts using mutual-information-based measures, a different method from the original neuron examples.
record.gate_note: The reported TabPFN neuron–concept saliency and selectivity results bear on single-concept interpretability. AUC results do not bear on the claim. The Pareto-front comparison with sparse probes is not extracted as a separate result because it compares the study’s search method with other methods.
record.test_reason: The study measures how selectively TabPFN neurons associate with ICD concept labels; it searches for single-concept 'grandmother cells'. It does not measure polysemanticity as any version defines it. TabPFN is a tabular model, not an image classifier (V1) or language model (V2). Superposition appears only as related-work background (V3). Capacity, initialization, architecture and measurement choices are not varied (V3–V5, V7). No candidate polysemantic neuron is re-examined for a shared underlying feature (V6). Selectivity below 1 across 24 correlated clinical labels is a related but different construct. It is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors report the first evidence that some TabPFN neurons show moderate, statistically significant saliency and selectivity for high-level concepts. They say such neurons can be found with a simple search, but found no 'grandmother cells' (selectivity ≤0.73).
record.recipe_differences: The study uses information-theoretic neuron–concept association measures on tabular-model embeddings, rather than the original visual neuron analysis or SoLU intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors note that selectivity tends to be higher for smaller concept sets and that results are not statistically significant on all tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: In TabPFN 2.0.9 on four MIMIC-IV-ED triage tasks, single-neuron selectivity for high-level ICD concepts peaks at 0.73. It is significant on only 2 of 4 tasks. No near-exclusive single-concept neurons were found, and most neurons were neither salient nor selective.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neurons in tabular foundation models rarely show near-exclusive selectivity for single labeled domain concepts.

record.peer_reviewed: EurIPS 2025 Workshop on AI for Tabular Data
record.problems: The study’s significance tests are asymptotic and assume i.i.d. scores, despite possible data scarcity and dependencies among layers and hierarchical concept labels. The authors note that the scores are not significant on all tasks and that selectivity is at most 0.73. The analysis selects knee points and does not establish that the associated features form a shared feature used by the network.
record.rows_left_out: The plotted Pareto-front points in Appendix C are not separately extracted; the paper does not tabulate their individual values, and the baseline-front comparison is a comparison of methods. AUC results are omitted because they do not bear on the claim.

untested.parts: No language model; TabPFN is a tabular foundation model.
Superposition is cited only as background; capacity is not varied.
Initialization, regularization and training noise are not studied.
No architecture, activation or regularization comparison.
No canonical polysemantic neuron is re-examined for a shared feature; prevalence of unrelated mixtures is not measured.
Activation range and explanation scoring are not varied. The authors do note that selectivity depends on concept-set size, but they do not test this.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' with a V6 limits_scope label is overturned. The study looks for monosemantic concept neurons via mutual information with ICD labels; it neither tests polysemanticity nor reinterprets polysemantic neurons. Knee points come from the study's own search, so the rows are selection values. The authors also note knee points appear across early, middle and final layers. This concerns layer distribution of concept neurons in a tabular model, not V2.

versions.untested_parts: No image classifier or vision neuron is tested.
No language model or token/context response is tested.
Superposition is discussed as background, but capacity pressure is not varied or tested.
Initialization, regularization, and training noise are not tested.
No architecture, activation function, or regularization comparison is made.

The study tests selectivity for labeled concepts in TabPFN, not canonical vision neurons, prevalence of truly unrelated mixtures, or whether the candidate neurons’ associated features share a causal feature used by the network.
The study does not vary activation range or explanation-scoring method to test measurement dependence.

rows.subject: TabPFN 2.0.9
rows.operation_detail: Measured mutual-information-based surprisal and selectivity for neuron–concept pairs; reported the knee point for ICU transfer within 12h.

conditions.value: Q (congenital malformations, deformations, and chromosomal abnormalities)

rows.note: The authors report statistical significance but describe selectivity as moderate and state that they did not identify neurons that almost exclusively respond to single concepts. The selected neuron’s top-3 features were ICU admissions in the past year, heart rate, and hypothyroidism.
rows.check: Mutual-information selectivity for ICD labels in a tabular model does not test V6. No polysemantic neuron is re-analysed for a shared feature. Also a knee point chosen by the study's own search, i.e. a selection value.

rows.subject: TabPFN 2.0.9
rows.operation_detail: Measured mutual-information-based surprisal and selectivity for neuron–concept pairs; reported the knee point for hospitalization.
rows.note: The authors suggest the neuron may encode high triage acuity, hypoxemia, and other signs of traumatic chest injury associated with transport accidents; this is a proposed interpretation, not a tested causal feature. The selected neuron’s top-3 features were hospitalizations in the past three months, oxygen saturation, and emergency severity index.
rows.check: Same as R1. The 'traumatic chest injury' reading is the authors' speculation, not a test that mixed responses share one feature. Knee-point selection value.

rows.subject: TabPFN 2.0.9
rows.operation_detail: Measured mutual-information-based surprisal and selectivity for neuron–concept pairs; reported the knee point for inhospital mortality.
rows.note: The combined result is statistically insignificant. The selected neuron’s top-3 features were ED visits in the past month, respiration rate, and dementia.
rows.check: Same as R1. Non-significant knee-point selection value; does not bear on any version.

rows.subject: TabPFN 2.0.9
rows.operation_detail: Measured mutual-information-based surprisal and selectivity for neuron–concept pairs; reported the knee point for critical outcome.
rows.note: The combined result is statistically insignificant. The selected neuron’s top-3 features were ED visits in the past three months, pain scale, and cardiac arrhythmia.
rows.check: Same as R1. Non-significant knee-point selection value; does not bear on any version.

rows.subject: TabPFN 2.0.9
rows.operation_detail: Summarized neuron–concept saliency and selectivity across the analyzed tasks.
rows.value: Most neurons were neither salient nor selective for specific ICD codes; maximum surprisal was log(N) = 7.74 and selectivity reached 0.73.
rows.note: These aggregate statements do not establish whether neurons with multiple responses encode one shared feature or unrelated features.
rows.check: The aggregate statement that most neurons were neither salient nor selective does not separate polysemantic neurons from neurons unrelated to the labels. It bears on no version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The study cites superposition and grandmother cells as motivation and does not test polysemanticity, so discusses fits.

tranche.reason: The study searches TabPFN neurons for single-concept saliency and selectivity on ICD labels. It does not measure whether neurons respond to unrelated inputs, so it tests no version. Superposition appears only as background in the related work. T6 fits; T3 is arguable but no version covers tabular models or this measure.

source_check.notes: All Table 1 values match the text. R1-R4 are knee points chosen by the study's own search (selection values). The 'traumatic chest injury' reading for neuron 49 is speculation ('may potentially encode'). The reader's call (tests, T2) was corrected to discusses, T6.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: TabPFN on the four ED triage tasks
reader_labels.reason: The selected neuron–concept pairs show at most moderate selectivity (0.73), and only two of four task knee points are significant; the study reports no near-exclusive single-concept neurons (R1–R5).
